extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community — grant applicants, investigators, institutional research administrators
extracted.subtask_description: A news/index page summarizing recent NIH extramural policy updates, resources, and guidance relevant to preparing and managing NIH grant applications and awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting appropriate research models
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators should still select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches and encourages approaches that enhance human relevance and translational potential. Choose models that are scientifically justified for the question being asked; preference is for approaches that improve human relevance and translation to human health.

rubrics_metrics.name: PF5 Collaborative International Research Projects: application format and key features
rubrics_metrics.description: Watch NIH’s 6-minute overview of the new Collaborative International Research Project (PF5) award structure to learn key features, application format, and how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should follow the PF5 application format and be aware that applications may be split into linked awards after peer review and prior to Just-in-Time, affecting how projects are funded and administered.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: We have issued a new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing DMS plans, use the 2026 Pilot format and include the simplified required elements specified by NIH. This is the format NIH expects for pilot DMS submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation to embed replication and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Embedding Replication and Reproducibility Throughout NIH Research: the reliability of biomedical research is foundational to public trust in science and to ensuring that findings can benefit patients and communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan and the new Replication and Reproducibility Initiative encourage applicants and awardees to incorporate replication and reproducibility practices into applications, study design, and research programs. Applicants should demonstrate how replication/reproducibility are addressed where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring outcome: 'Competitive But Not Discussed' category
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizing that strong applications may fall below a 33% cut off, the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as 'competitive but not discussed.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Following emergency modifications to review processes, applications falling in the middle third may be scored 'competitive but not discussed' (i.e., not discussed in full study section). Applicants should understand this scoring classification and its relation to percentile/cutoff practices used in peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralized peer review considerations and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: All peer review was centralized within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR); consolidation has initial effects on the peer-review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and institutions should be aware that centralized peer review aims to strengthen efficiency, competition, and transparency; changes from consolidation may affect review timelines, study section assignment, and competitive dynamics.
